issues.description: Behavior change in panLinear/zoomLinear: identity used to pass through originals; coerceNumber now coerces and substitutes 0 for null/undefined.
issues.detail: Previously panLinear/zoomLinear used `identity` as the ground function, returning the exact lifted values. The lift was `toNumber` (which could return null). Now lift is `coerceNumber` which substitutes 0 for null/undefined inputs, silently changing outputs for non-numeric domain entries (e.g. Date objects, strings) that previously round-tripped via toNumber+identity.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the empty-domain check, producing NaN sign instead of throwing for [].
issues.detail: `panLog`/`zoomLog` call `Math.sign(domain[0])` before invoking pan/zoom, so for an empty domain the sign is computed on `undefined` (NaN) before the `isNonEmpty` guard fires inside pan/zoom. The error still throws, but the ordering is fragile and only the Linear variants are tested for the empty case.

issues.description: Runtime empty-domain error is a new throw that may break existing callers depending on prior NaN-returning behavior.
issues.detail: The PR description acknowledges this is a behavior change. Previously empty domains returned `[NaN, NaN]` rather than throwing. Downstream consumers in vega-scale or user code that defensively handle NaN results will now see an exception. This should be called out in a changeset/release notes and confirmed acceptable.

issues.description: Domain return type narrowed to [number, number] but lift/ground may produce NaN; type is misleading.
issues.detail: `Domain = [number, number]` doesn't capture that log/pow transforms can produce NaN (e.g. log of negative, pow of negative with fractional exponent). Callers relying on the type may be surprised. Consider documenting or using `number` without implying validity.

issues.description: Local `identity` shadows the removed import from `./accessors.js` with a number-only signature.
issues.detail: The previous code imported `identity` from accessors, which is generic. The new local `identity: TransformFn` is number-only. Functionally equivalent here, but the naming collision with the exported `accessors.identity` could confuse future readers. A comment clarifying why a local variant is used would help.

issues.description: peek overload `readonly [T, ...T[]]` matches NonEmptyArray but pan/zoom pass `number[]` after a type guard; verify narrowing flows.
issues.detail: After `isNonEmpty(domain)` the variable is narrowed to `NonEmptyArray<number>` inside pan/zoom, so `peek(domain)` should pick the non-undefined overload. Confirm TS actually selects the non-undefined overload here; otherwise `d1` remains `number | undefined` and arithmetic still type-errors or coerces silently.

review.summary: The refactor is mostly mechanical typing, but the swap from `identity` (ground) + `toNumber` (lift) to `coerceNumber` + local number-only `identity` changes semantics for non-numeric domain entries by substituting 0 for null. The new empty-domain throw is a real behavior change and should be flagged in release notes; tests only cover the Linear variants. Log/Pow variants still read `domain[0]` before the guard, which is fragile. Types are tighter but `Domain = [number, number]` overstates validity since transforms can return NaN.
